statement: BC should balance its budget even in uncertain economic times, cutting spending to get there.

passages.title: Hansard 43-2, Issue 127 (Feb 26 2026 pm) - Second Reading, Bill 5 Trade Recognition Act (Valeriote)
passages.quote: Reducing interprovincial trade barriers is not just sound economic policy. It strengthens our resilience in these uncertain economic times. It strengthens our unity as a country, and it strengthens our independence in a world where global economic conditions are increasingly unpredictable. At a time when supply chains can be disrupted by events beyond our control and trade tensions can emerge overnight, Canada’s greatest economic strength should be Canada itself.

passages.title: BC Greens Plan Free Childcare Expansion and Name Greater Victoria Candidate (West Coast Current)
passages.quote: The debate signals a broader transition in campaign topics, moving toward resource development and cost-of-living concerns. While Doerkson framed his approach around reducing regulatory delays and avoiding tax increases, NDP Leader David Eby was in Prince Rupert making his party’s case for the resource sector. The NDP also targeted Conservative fiscal plans, raising past comments from Conservative MLA Tony Luck regarding potential spending reductions to major budget items like healthcare. Doerkson firmly rejected those claims, stating he has no intention of cutting health funding.

passages.title: BC Greens propose comprehensive policies to address BC's drug poisoning crisis
passages.quote: Just as prohibition in the 1920s led to the increased potency of alcohol, the war on drugs continues to drive up ever-increasing levels of toxicity in street substances. To avoid and evade shifting law enforcement strategies, the drug supply is systematically changing, unpredictable, and contains wide-ranging cutting agents. It has been nearly a decade since fentanyl replaced heroin as the primary street opioid available in BC. Fentanyl, a word that North Americans have become far too familiar with, is estimated to be 20-40 times more potent than heroin, and 100 times more potent than morphine.
